speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how does the Ministry ensure that there are sufficient engineering graduates from our Institutes of Higher Learning to meet the projected needs for rail engineering and the opening of the Thomson-East Coast Line; and (b) whether the Ministry has plans to train young engineers to develop "deep engineering expertise" as recommended by SMRT's technical advisory panel and, if so, what are these plans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This was one of the first initiatives that I launched when I joined MOT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I see this growing need for greater expertise in this area and I have not even talked about the HSR and RTS yet. "Deep expertise" is the most valuable currency in the railway industry.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is an important framework because then, everybody, all the stakeholders, will know what to do as we go forward.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Framework provides consistent industry-wide standards on the skills and competencies required at different levels in the railway sector and the corresponding training courses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With this, training institutions can better design their curricula to cater to the attainment of different skill levels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Employers can also use this framework to put in place structured on-the-job skills development programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Students and workers seeking to upgrade themselves will also have information on the programmes available to help them reach the next skill level and concrete milestones to work towards.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At the same time, we are also stepping up training efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We are also working with programme partners to launch more rail-related Continuing Education and Training programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: For example, Singapore Polytechnic has launched the Earn-And-Learn programme that enables ITE graduates who are working in the rail industry to upgrade their skills by taking courses that can eventually add up to a diploma.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: NTU has just introduced a new Specialist Certificate in Civil Infrastructure Engineering to help environmental engineers gain civil engineering knowledge.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Based on what the Minister has shared about on-the-job training, I would like to understand when he mentioned "deep engineering expertise", may I know what is the proportion that can be accomplished through classroom training?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How much on-the-job training is required and, if a lot of on-the-job training is required, do we currently have sufficient experienced engineers to provide the on-the-job training to the young engineers?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Clearly, middle-level mentors are in short supply because, especially when we are in such an accelerated programme of trying to do so many things.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Therefore, the traditional or tertiary institutions play a major role but we will do what we can.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: By "deep expertise", I also have in mind the higher end of the eco-system because the whole rail industry, not just in Singapore, world-wide, is transforming.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: One of the first things I observed when I joined MOT was how backward the rail industry was compared to the other transport sectors, like aviation and shipping, worldwide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Aviation is way ahead, shipping is behind and railway engineering is really, really behind.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I was, for example, looking at the way they maintained things.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I spent quite some time visiting the aviation industry, how do they do their maintenance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And I have been pushing, for example, for predictive maintenance and it was still a very new concept for the railway operators.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I said, not just in Singapore but world-wide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, even though we have tonnes of problems trying to resolve the immediate basic needs of upgrading maintenance, I tell my stakeholders to also look far ahead.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The rail industry globally is a sunrise industry.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is just between Malaysia and Singapore but hundreds and thousands of kilometres of HSRs are being built in Asia.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: You look at the Belt and Road Initiatives.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Singaporeans who have that kind of interest and, given the opportunities, I think we should try to gain a slice of that opportunity.
